rule: No synthetic interview quotations. Distinguish source-derived qualitative themes from future primary fieldwork.

source_derived_themes.theme: Verification becomes part of professional AI use
source_derived_themes.evidence: Experienced GenAI users in ILO Poland focus groups tended to regard checking AI outputs as an ordinary part of work.
source_derived_themes.use: Supports 'judgement' as a skill; present as qualitative theme.

source_derived_themes.theme: Skill erosion and creativity are lived concerns
source_derived_themes.evidence: Occasional GenAI users in the ILO qualitative research expressed more concern about loss of creativity and erosion of underlying skills.
source_derived_themes.use: Human tension in New Advantage; do not attach prevalence unless source provides it.

source_derived_themes.theme: AI adoption can outrun organisational governance
source_derived_themes.evidence: Formal employer introduction (9.4%) lagged reported personal use in the previous week (16.7%) in the Polish worker survey.
Workers in workplaces that introduced GenAI with consultation reported more use and appetite for more use; opposition was higher where dialogue was absent.
source_derived_themes.use: Shows organisational design is part of AI's labour impact.

primary_fieldwork_goal: Collect original accounts of how AI changes task allocation, expectations of junior staff, learning pathways, quality control, workload and perceived capture of productivity gains.
recommended_sample: 12–20 semi-structured interviews across early-career workers/students, mid-career professionals, senior practitioners/managers and hiring/recruiting roles. Seek variation in AI adoption rather than statistical representativeness.
